review_metadata.scope: Implementation review — API alignment, test quality, runtime boundary, isolation
review_metadata.previous_round: Round 1 Claude review flagged MockMC API misalignment, layer mapping gaps, missing override logic

mockmc_api_alignment.details: MockMC now matches real MemoryController API exactly

commit_signature.mock: commit(*a, **kw) — extracts mission_id, key, content, kind, evidence_id, confidence from kw args
commit_signature.real: commit(mission_id, key, content, kind, evidence_id=None, confidence=1.0, ...)
commit_signature.call_style_in_code: All calls use keyword args: commit(mission_id=..., key=..., content=..., kind=..., evidence_id=..., confidence=...)
commit_signature.verdict: MATCH — keyword-arg calling convention fully compatible

recall_signature.call_style_in_code: recall(mission_id, layer='semantic') — positional mission_id, keyword layer

layer_mapping.details: Layer mapping correctly maps kind→layer via _LAYER_MAP in both test files
layer_mapping.note: Test layer map is self-consistent but see CRITICAL finding below about 'experience' kind not existing in real ConsolidationRules

get_preference_returns_most_recent.details: Iterates all records, reassigns `found = r` on each match, last match wins. Since MockMC appends to list, last = most recent. Test test_update_overwrites confirms this behavior.

evidence_backed_override.details: resolve_conflict sets new_score = 99.0 when evidence_id is truthy, guaranteeing override over any old_score (max theoretical ~1.0). Test test_evidence_backed_overrides confirms: weak pref (weight=0.9, conf=0.9, old_score=0.81) is overridden by strong pref with evidence_id='ev_strong'.

critical_findings.title: Layer mismatch: experience_learner writes to 'semantic' but reads from 'episodic' in production
critical_findings.detail: experience_learner.record_outcome() commits with kind='experience'. The real MemoryController._classify_layer() calls classify_layer('experience') which returns 'semantic' (default for unknown kinds — 'experience' is NOT in KIND_TO_LAYER). However, extract_patterns(), rank_experiences(), and prune_irrelevant() all call rank_retrieve() with layers=['episodic']. In production, experiences would be stored in the semantic layer but retrieved from the episodic layer — they would NEVER be found.
critical_findings.root_cause: Test MockMC maps 'experience' → 'episodic' in its _LAYER_MAP, masking this bug. Real ConsolidationRules.KIND_TO_LAYER has no 'experience' key — classify_layer('experience') returns 'semantic' (default).
affected_methods: extract_patterns() — reads layers=['episodic'], but records stored in 'semantic'
rank_experiences() — reads layers=['episodic'], but records stored in 'semantic'
prune_irrelevant() — reads layers=['episodic'], but records stored in 'semantic'
fix_options: Option A: Add 'experience' → 'episodic' to ConsolidationRules.KIND_TO_LAYER (best — semantically correct, episodic is for time-bounded events)
Option B: Change experience_learner queries to use layers=['semantic'] (wrong — semantically incorrect)
Option C: Change experience_learner to use kind='decision' or kind='failure' per outcome (requires refactor of record_outcome)
critical_findings.recommended_fix: Option A — Add 'experience': 'episodic' to KIND_TO_LAYER in consolidation_rules.py

critical_findings.title: Two pattern extraction tests have zero assertions (vacuously passing)
critical_findings.detail: test_extract_success_pattern (line 88-91) and test_extract_failure_pattern (line 93-96) call learner.extract_patterns() but have NO assert statements. They pass trivially because Python functions without assertions cannot fail. These tests provide zero coverage verification.
critical_findings.recommended_fix: Add assertions verifying extracted pattern properties: pattern_type ('tool_selection_success' for high success rate), success_rate correctness, frequency count

critical_findings.title: apply_decay ignores half_life_hours parameter
critical_findings.detail: PreferenceModel.apply_decay() accepts half_life_hours: int = 168 but always applies a flat 0.99 multiplier to weight regardless of parameter value. The half-life semantics documented in the docstring ('Decay preferences older than half-life') are not implemented.
critical_findings.evidence: Line 73: new_weight = p.weight * (1.0 - 0.01) — constant 0.99, half_life_hours never used
critical_findings.recommended_fix: Either implement time-based decay using half_life_hours and p.created_at, or remove the parameter if flat decay is intentional

critical_findings.title: Duplicate MockMC class in both test files
critical_findings.detail: test_preference_model.py (lines 9-52) and test_experience_learner.py (lines 9-52) contain identical MockMC implementations including identical _LAYER_MAP. This violates DRY and means fixes to MockMC must be applied in two places.
critical_findings.recommended_fix: Extract MockMC to tests/brain/phase2b/conftest.py or tests/brain/phase2b/mock_mc.py

record_outcome.alignment: STRUCTURALLY CORRECT but kind='experience' is not a real MemoryKind (CF-001)

extract_patterns.logic: Groups by action, requires >=3 samples, classifies as tool_selection_success (>70%), decision_path_outcome (<30%), or timing_pattern (30-70%)

rank_experiences.bonus_penalty_logic: Success experiences get +10% confidence boost, failures get -5%. Clamped to [0.1, 1.0].

prune_irrelevant.note: Returns count only, doesn't actually prune. Method name is aspirational.

mock_fidelity.mockmc_recall_global_behavior: MockMC.recall() treats mission_id='global' as 'return all missions'. Real MC passes mission_id directly to DB — no global wildcard. PreferenceModel uses mission_id='global' as default in get_all_preferences/get_profile. This could produce different results in production if 'global' isn't handled by DB layer.
mock_fidelity.mockmc_evidence_enforcement: MockMC does NOT enforce evidence binding (real MC raises ValueError for preference without evidence_id). Tests always pass non-empty evidence_ids, so this gap doesn't cause false positives, but it means the enforcement logic is untested.
mock_fidelity.mockmc_rank_retrieve_scoring: MockMC uses simplistic keyword substring matching. Real MC uses relevance (0.5) + recency (0.25) + confidence (0.25) weighted scoring. This means test ranking order may differ from production ranking order.

preference_model.resolve_conflict_empty_string_edge_case: If evidence_id='' (empty string), new_score = confidence (not 99.0). This is consistent with record_preference converting None→'' but could surprise callers.
preference_model.get_preference_ordering_dependency: Relies on iteration order matching insertion order. Real MC recall() may return DB-ordered results. If DB doesn't preserve insertion order, 'most recent' guarantee breaks.
preference_model.deserialize_pref_fallback: Correctly falls back to record-level weight/confidence/evidence_id if not found in serialized content JSON.

experience_learner.record_outcome_confidence: Sets confidence=0.5 for success, 0.3 for failure — appropriate differentiation.
experience_learner.extract_patterns_min_samples: Requires >=3 samples per action before pattern is emitted — reasonable statistical threshold.
experience_learner.rank_experiences_bonus_logic: Success experiences get 1.1x confidence boost, failures get 0.95x penalty. Sort key is confidence * (1.5 if success else 0.5). Reasonable but could use configurable weights.
experience_learner.prune_irrelevant: Returns count but doesn't actually delete/prune. Method name is misleading — should be renamed to count_low_confidence or similar.
experience_learner.summarize_limit: Calls extract_patterns(limit=20) — lower limit than default 50, reasonable for summary use.

verdict.round1_fixes: ALL FIXES CONFIRMED — MockMC API alignment, layer mapping, get_preference most-recent, evidence-backed override
verdict.new_issues: 1 HIGH (CF-001 layer mismatch), 2 MEDIUM (CF-002 no-assertion tests, CF-003 dead parameter), 1 LOW (CF-004 code duplication)
verdict.overall_assessment: CONDITIONAL PASS — Round 1 fixes are solid and verifiable. However, CF-001 is a production bug masked by test mock: experience_learner writes to semantic layer but reads from episodic layer. Tests pass because MockMC maps 'experience' → 'episodic', but the real ConsolidationRules default unknown kinds to 'semantic'. Fix CF-001 before production deployment. CF-002 (no-assertion tests) should be fixed to ensure the pattern extraction pipeline is actually tested. CF-003 (unused half_life_hours) is a code quality issue. The module boundary (no runtime imports, no brain.db imports) is clean and well-verified by 4 isolation tests.
recommended_actions: P0: Add 'experience': 'episodic' to KIND_TO_LAYER in consolidation_rules.py (fix CF-001)
P1: Add assertions to test_extract_success_pattern and test_extract_failure_pattern (fix CF-002)
P2: Implement or remove half_life_hours parameter in apply_decay (fix CF-003)
P3: Extract shared MockMC to conftest.py (fix CF-004)
P3: Add test for preference without evidence_id behavior (evidence enforcement verification)
P3: Add test for resolve_conflict when low-confidence challenger loses
